summary_html: A **state agency fails** to meet federal child-welfare performance standards, triggering **funding penalties** or corrective action under the CFSR or Single Audit Act.
authority_html:
- **Child & Family Services Reviews (45 CFR Part 1355)** — performance oversight and penalties  
- **Single Audit Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 7501–7507)** — audit of federally funded programs  
- **Inspector General Act (5 U.S.C. App.)** — oversight authority for HHS/OIG

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In re D.F., H.F., M.F. and D.F., Juveniles
key_cases.holding: Termination of the father's rights was affirmed notwithstanding his completion of case-plan tasks, and his separate challenge to the standalone reasonable-efforts finding was dismissed as moot once termination was upheld.
key_cases.relevance: D.F. identifies the reasonable-efforts finding under 33 V.S.A. § 5321(h) as the mechanism preserving federal funding, and holds a parent's challenge to it moot once termination stands.
key_cases.quote: A reasonable-efforts finding is essential to preserving federal funding for state child-welfare programs.

key_cases.holding: Termination was affirmed; a reasonable-efforts finding is a separate determination from the best-interests inquiry and is not a precondition to terminating parental rights, although the level of assistance given to parents remains relevant to whether they can resume parenting in a reasonable time.
key_cases.relevance: C.P. separates the federally driven reasonable-efforts finding from the state-law merits of termination, so a federal compliance lapse does not automatically invalidate the state outcome.
key_cases.quote: the court is not required to find DCF made reasonable efforts as a prerequisite to termination

key_cases.case_name: In re Appeal of T.O. & L.O.
key_cases.holding: The Human Services Board lacked jurisdiction over grandparents' claim that DCF failed to comply with state and federal relative-placement requirements; their remedy lies in the family division of the superior court, and no due process violation resulted.
key_cases.relevance: The case addresses alleged non-compliance with federally conditioned relative-notice requirements and holds the administrative forum unavailable to remedy it.
key_cases.quote: That procedure is access to the family division, not to the Human Services Board.

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Date the administrative reviewer sent notice of the decision on the substantiation review (33 V.S.A. § 4916a(i)); the review itself must be requested within 30 days after the Department sent notice of the right to review (33 V.S.A. § 4916a(c)(1))
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: If no review by the Human Services Board is requested, the Department's decision is final and the person has no further right of review under this section; the Board may grant a waiver upon good cause shown (33 V.S.A. § 4916b(d)).
